messages.subject: rqtl est.map recalculation
parts:
Hello,

I am constructing genetic maps. During my process, (following your tutorial - very helpful!), after calculating the best marker order, I do est.map to look at the genetic locations.
I sometimes need to remove outlying markers and then continue building the genetic map without them. In that case, i run
newmap <- est.map(data_cross, error.prob=0.005)
data_cross <- replace.map(data_cross, newmap)

to look at the change, i run the two commands: 
1. plotMap(data_cross, show.marker.names=TRUE)
2. pull.map(data_cross, chr=1)

Unexpected results occur when one of the outlying markers is from the first genetic position (0cM). In that case, plotMap indeed shows me a new marker at position 0cM, however pull.map (and also geno.table(data_cross, scanone.output=TRUE)) 
show that now the marker at position 1 (e.g formerly positioned 3rd), remains in its former location and not relocated to be at 0cM. In fact, my entire recalculated map begins not at 0cM but, for example, at 100cM . 

Is it possible est.map somehow remembers the old positions? How can I fix this that all new positioned are once again relative to 0cM even after removing the original first marker?

Thank you for your help

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: rqtl est.map recalculation
parts:
The first marker on each chromosome gets left in its position, but what really matters are the distances between markers. plotMap() will shift all chromosomes to start at 0; use the argument shift=FALSE to avoid that.

There's a function shiftmap() that you can use to shift all chromosomes on a map to start at 0.

    newmap <- shiftmap(newmap)

You separately asked about replace.map and replacemap. These are synonyms...they do the same thing.

karl
